6124.text: If the angle between the curves $y=e^{2(1+x)-4}$ and $x^2 y=1$ at the point $(1,1)$ is $\theta$, then $|\sin \theta|+|\cos \theta|=$
6124.sol:
Given the curves $y=e^{2(1+x)-4}$ and $x^2 y=1$
Now $y=e^{2(1+x)-4} \Rightarrow y^{\prime}=2 e^{2 x-2}y^{\prime}(1)=2=m_1$
and $x^2 y=1 \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{x^2}\Rightarrow y^{\prime}=\frac{-2}{x^3} \Rightarrow y^{\prime}(1)=+2=m_2$
Since, $\tan \theta=\left|\frac{2-(-2)}{1+2(-2)}\right| \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{4}{3}$
So $|\sin \theta|+|\cos \theta|=\frac{4}{5}+\frac{3}{5}=\frac{7}{5}$

7038.text:
The equation of the circle which cuts the circles
$\begin{aligned}
& S_1 \equiv x²+y²-4=0 \\

at$ the extremities of diameters of these circles is
7038.sol:
Let the equation of required circle is
\(S \equiv x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0\)
and equation of given circles
$\begin{aligned}
& S_1 \equiv x²+y²-4=0 \\
& S_2 \equiv x²+y²-6 x-8 y+10=0 \\
& S_3=x²+y²+2 x-4 y-2=0
\end{aligned}$
\(\because\) Circle \(S=0\) cuts the circles \(S_1=0, S_2=0\) and \(S_3=0\) at the extermities of the diameters, so common chord of \(S=0\) and \(S_1=0\) passes through the centre of the circle \(S_1=0\), so \(c=-4\)
Similarly \((2 g+6) x+(2 f+8) y-14=0\) passes through \((3,4)\), so \(6 g+8 f+36=0\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad 3 g+4 f+18=0\)...(i)
and \((2 g-2) x+(2 f+4) y-2=0\), passes through \((-1,2)\), so
\(-2 g+4 f+8=0\)...(ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\((g, f)=(-2,-3)\)
So equation of required circle is
\(x²+y²-4 x-6 y-4=0\)

8409.subject: Mathematics
8409.text: If $a \ne b, x \ne n\pi, n \in Z$ and $y^{2} = a^{2}\cos^{2}x + b^{2}\sin^{2}x,$ then $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + y =$
8409.sol:
It is given that,

$a \ne b, x \ne n\pi, n \in z$ and $y^{2} = a^{2}\cos^{2}x + b^{2}\sin^{2}x$

Differentiate the above equation w.r.t. $x$,

$2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - a^{2}sin2x + b^{2}sin2x$

$2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)sin2x$

Again differentiate the above equation w.r.t. $x$,

$2\left(y\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2\right) = 2\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x$

$y\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2 = \left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x$

Multiply $y^{2}$ on both sides,

$y^{3}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + y^{2}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2 = y^{2}\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x$

$y^{3}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = y^{2}\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x - y^{2}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2$

Add $y^{4}$ in the above equation.

$y^{4} + y^{3}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = y^{4} + y^{2}\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x - y^{2}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2$

Substitute the values in the above equation.

$y^{4} + y^{3}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = y^{4} + y^{2}\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)cos2x - y^{2}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2$

$= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\left(a^{2}\cos^{2}x + b^{2}\sin^{2}x\right)\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)\left(\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x\right) - \\ \left(\left(b^{2} - a^{2}\right)sinxcosx\right)2 + \left(a^{2}\cos^{2}x + b^{2}\sin^{2}x\right)2\end{array}\right\}$

$= a^{2}b^{2}\cos^{4}x + a^{2}b^{2}\sin^{2}x + 2a^{2}b^{2}\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x$

$= a^{2}b^{2}\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)2$

$= a^{2}b^{2}$

Or it can be written as,

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + y = \dfrac{1}{y}\left(\dfrac{ab}{y}\right)2$

10869.text: A bag $P$ contains 5 white marbles and 3 black marbles. Four marbles are drawn at random from $P$ and are put in an empty bag $Q$. If a marble drawn at random from $Q$ is found to be black then the probability that all the three black marbles in $P$ are transfered to the bag $Q$ is.
10869.sol:
Here, $W=$ White, $B=$ Black. Given that bag $P$ contains $5 W$ marbles and $3 B$ marbles. 4 marbles are drawn from the bag $P$ and A$ black marble is drawn from bag $Q$.
Let Event $E_1: 1 $\mathrm{ W}$ and $3 \mathrm{ B}$ marbles are transferred Event $E_2: 2 \mathrm{ W}$ and 2 $\mathrm{ B} marbles are transferred Event $E_3: 3 $\mathrm{ W}$ and 1 $\mathrm{ B} marbles are transferred Event $E_4: 4 $\mathrm{ W}$ and 0 $\mathrm{ B} marbles are transferred$ and Event A : a black marble is drawn from bag $Q$.
Then, $P\left(E_1\right)=\frac{{ }^5 C_1 \times{ }^3 C_3}{{ }^8 C_4}=\frac{5}{{ }^8 C_4}
 \begin{aligned}& P\left(E_2\right)=\frac{{ }^5 C_2 \times{ }^3 C_2}{{ }^8 C_4}=\frac{30}{{ }^8 C_4}\\
& P\left(E_3\right)=\frac{{ }^5 C_3 \times{ }^3 C_1}{{ }^8 C_4}=\frac{30}{{ }^8 C_4}\\
& P\left(E_4\right)=\frac{{ }^5 C_4 \times{ }^3 C_0}{{ }^8 C_4}=\frac{5}{{ }^8 C_4}
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}& P\left(A / E_1\right)=\frac{3}{4}\\
& P\left(A / E_2\right)=\frac{2}{4}\\
& P\left(A / E_3\right)=\frac{1}{4}\\
& P\left(A / E_4\right)=0
\end{aligned}

By using Bayes' theorem,

\begin{aligned}P\left(E_1 / A\right)=& \frac{P\left(E_1\right)\cdot P \left(A / E_1\right)}{\left(P\left(E_1\right)\cdot P \left(A / E_1\right)+P\left(E_2\right)\cdot P \left(A / E_2\right)\right.}\\
 +P\left(E_3\right)P\left(A / E_3\right)+P\left(E_4\right)\cdotP\left(A / E_4\right)\\
=  \frac{\frac{5}{{ }^8 C_4} \cdot \frac{3}{4}}{\frac{5}{{ }^8 C_4} \cdot \frac{3}{4}+\frac{30}{{ }^8 C_4} \times \frac{2}{4}+\frac{30}{{ }^8 C_4} \times \frac{1}{4}+0}\\
=  \frac{15}{15+60+30}=\frac{15}{105}=\frac{1}{7}
\end{aligned}$

11895.text: A point on the straight line $3 x+5 y=15$ which is equidistant from the coordinate axes will lie in
options: either in the $3^{\text{rd }}$ or in the $4^{\text{th }}$ quadrant
11895.sol:
Let $P$ be the point which is equidistant from the coordinate axis.
$\therefore \quad P$ lies on the line $y=x or y=-x$.
Let us find intersecting point of $3 x+5 y=15 and y=x$ for this,
$3 x+5 x=15 \Rightarrow 8 x=15 \Rightarrow x=\frac{15}{8}$
So, $y=x=\frac{15}{8}\therefore$ Intersection point of $\left(\frac{15}{8}, \frac{15}{8}\right)$, which is in first quadrant.
Now, let us find the intersecting point of $3 x+5 y=15 and y=-x$ for this
$\Rightarrow 3 x-5 x=15 \Rightarrow-2 x=15 \Rightarrow x=\frac{-15}{2}$
So, $y=-x=\frac{15}{2}\therefore$ Intersecting point is $\left(-\frac{15}{2}, \frac{15}{2}\right)$, which is in 2nd quadrant.

& \Rightarrow \sqrt{3}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{2}-\frac{1}{2} y\right)^2-4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x-y}{2}\right) \\
& \left(\frac{x+\sqrt{3} y}{2}\right)+\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{x+\sqrt{3} y}{2}\right)^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{3}\left(3 x^2-2 \sqrt{3} x y+y^2\right)-4\left(\sqrt{3} x^2+3 x y-x y-\sqrt{3} y^2\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3 \sqrt{3} x^2-6 x y+\sqrt{3} y^2-4 \sqrt{3} x^2-12 x y \\

16940.text: If the ratio of amplitudes of two interfering waves is $4: 3$, then the ratio of maximum and minimum intensity is
16940.sol:
Given, the ratio of amplitudes of two interfering waves is $4: 3$
i.e $\frac{A_1}{A_2}=\frac{4}{3}$ ...(i)
We know that, intensity of wave is proportional to square of amplitude.
$\therefore \frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\left(\frac{A_{\max }}{A_{\min }}\right)^2$, where maximum and minimum amplitudes are
$A_{\text{max }}=A_1+A_2$
and $\quad A_{\min }=A_1-A_2$
Substituting the values, we get
$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\left(\frac{A_1+A_2}{A_1-A_2}\right)^2$
Multiplying and dividing by $A_2^2$ in RHS, we get.
$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\left(\frac{\frac{A_1}{A_2}+1}{\frac{A_1}{A_2}-1}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\frac{4}{3}+1}{\frac{4}{3}-1}\right)^2=\left(\frac{7}{1}\right)^2=\frac{49}{1}$

20056.subject: Chemistry
20056.text: Which one of the following species will impart colour to an aqueous solution?
20056.sol:
The colour of transition metal ions in aqueous solution is due to d-d transitions, which require the presence of unpaired d-electrons (partially filled d-subshell).

The electronic configurations of the given ions are:
$\text{Cr}^{3+}$ (Z = 24): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3$ (3 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Cu}^+$ (Z = 29): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$ (0 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$ (Z = 30): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$ (0 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Ti}^{4+}$ (Z = 22): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$ (0 unpaired electrons)

Since $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ has a partially filled d-subshell, it will undergo d-d transitions and impart colour to the aqueous solution. The other ions have either empty or completely filled d-subshells and are colourless.

Answer: $\text{Cr}^{3+}$

20400.subject: Chemistry
20400.text:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
(I) Chlorobenzene
(II) Nitrobenzene
(III) Benzene
(IV) Isopropylbenzene
20400.sol: The reactivity of benzene derivatives towards electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the nature of the substituent attached to the benzene ring. Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density of the ring, making it more reactive, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease the electron density, making it less reactive.Analyzing the substituents:1. Isopropylbenzene (IV): The isopropyl group ($-CH(CH_3)_2$) is an alkyl group. It acts as an electron-donating group through the inductive effect (+I) and hyperconjugation, which significantly activates the benzene ring.2. Benzene (III): This is the reference compound with no substituents.3. Chlorobenzene (I): The chlorine atom is an electron-withdrawing group due to its strong inductive effect (-I), although it is ortho/para directing due to resonance (+M). Overall, it deactivates the ring compared to benzene.4. Nitrobenzene (II): The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a very strong electron-withdrawing group due to both -I and -M effects, which strongly deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution.Comparing the effects:Isopropylbenzene is more reactive than benzene because of the +I and hyperconjugation effects of the alkyl group. Benzene is more reactive than chlorobenzene because the -I effect of chlorine deactivates the ring. Chlorobenzene is more reactive than nitrobenzene because the -NO$_2$ group is a much stronger electron-withdrawing group than the chlorine atom.Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is: Isopropylbenzene > Benzene > Chlorobenzene > Nitrobenzene.Answer: $\text{ IV }>\text{ III }>\text{ I }>$$\text{ II }$

20556.subject: Chemistry
20556.text:
When $3.92 \mathrm{ g}$ of Mohr salt is dissolved in $100 \mathrm{ mL}$ of water, and titrated against $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ solution, $20 \mathrm{ mL}$ of this solution required $18 \mathrm{ mL}$ of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ for complete oxidation. The strength of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is:
[Molar mass of Mohr salt is $392 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is $158 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$]
20556.sol:
The molarity of the Mohr salt solution is calculated as follows:

Moles of Mohr salt = $\dfrac{3.92 \text{ g}}{392 \text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Molarity of Mohr salt solution = $\dfrac{0.01 \text{ mol}}{0.1 \text{ L}} = 0.1 \text{ M}$.

The reaction between $\text{KMnO}_4$ and Mohr salt in acidic medium is:
$\text{MnO}_4^{-} + 8\textH^{+} + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

The n-factor for Mohr salt ($\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}$) is 1, and for $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($\text{Mn}^{+7} \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2}$) is 5.

Using the equivalence relation $N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2$ for the titration of 20 mL of Mohr salt solution:
$N_{\text{Mohr}} \times 20 \text{ mL} = N_{\text{KMnO}_4} \times 18 \text{ mL}$.

Since $N_{\text{Mohr}} = M_{\text{Mohr}} \times 1 = 0.1 \text{ N}$, we have:
$0.1 \times 20 = N_{\text{KMnO}_4} \times 18$.

$N_{\text{KMnO}_4} = \dfrac{2}{18} = \dfrac{1}{9} \text{ N}$.

The molarity of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $M_{\text{KMnO}_4} = \dfrac{N_{\text{KMnO}_4}}{5} = \dfrac{1}{9 \times 5} = \dfrac{1}{45} \text{ M}$.

The strength of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in g/L is $M_{\text{KMnO}_4} \times \text{Molar mass} = \dfrac{1}{45} \times 158 \approx 3.51 \text{ g/L}$.

Rounding to the nearest option, the strength is 3.5 g/L.

Answer: 3.5 g/L

21893.subject: Mathematics
21893.text: Three fair dice are thrown. What is the probability of getting a total of 15 given that they exhibit three different numbers that are in arithmetic progression?
21893.sol:
Let the three numbers on the dice be $x, y, z$. The condition is that $x, y, z$ are in arithmetic progression and are distinct. Let the numbers be $a-d, a, a+d$ where $d > 0$.

Since the numbers are between $1$ and $6$, we have $1 \le a-d$ and $a+d \le 6$.

For $d=1$: $(a-1, a, a+1)$ can be $(1,2,3), (2,3,4), (3,4,5), (4,5,6)$. There are $4$ sets. Each set has $3! = 6$ permutations. Total outcomes = $4 \times 6 = 24$.

For $d=2$: $(a-2, a, a+2)$ can be $(1,3,5), (2,4,6)$. There are $2$ sets. Each set has $3! = 6$ permutations. Total outcomes = $2 \times 6 = 12$.

Total number of outcomes with three different numbers in arithmetic progression is $24 + 12 = 36$.

Now, we find the number of these outcomes that sum to $15$. The sum is $(a-d) + a + (a+d) = 3a = 15$, which implies $a = 5$.

For $a=5$, the possible sets are:
If $d=1$, the set is $(4, 5, 6)$. Permutations are $(4,5,6), (4,6,5), (5,4,6), (5,6,4), (6,4,5), (6,5,4)$. There are $6$ such outcomes.
If $d=2$, the set is $(3, 5, 7)$, but $7 > 6$, so this is not possible.

The number of favorable outcomes is $6$.

The probability is $\dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{1}{6}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{6}$

22837.subject: Physics
22837.text: Five charges, '$q$' each are placed at the comers of a regular pentagon of side '$a$' as shown in figure. First, charge from '$A$' is removed with other charges intact, then charge at '$A$' is replaced with an equal opposite charge. The ratio of magnitudes of electric fields at $\mathrm{O}$, without charge at $A$ and that with equal and opposite charge at $A$ is
22837.sol:
Let the electric field due to a charge $q$ at a corner of the regular pentagon at the center $O$ be $\vec{E}$. The distance from each corner to the center $O$ is $r$.

By symmetry, the sum of the electric fields due to all five charges $q$ at the corners $A, B, C, D, E$ is zero, i.e., $\vec{E}_A + \vec{E}_B + \vec{E}_C + \vec{E}_D + \vec{E}_E = 0$.

When the charge at $A$ is removed, the net electric field at $O$ is $\vec{E}_{net, 1} = \vec{E}_B + \vec{E}_C + \vec{E}_D + \vec{E}_E$. From the symmetry condition, $\vec{E}_{net, 1} = -\vec{E}_A$. The magnitude is $|\vec{E}_{net, 1}| = E$, where $E = \dfrac{kq}{r^2}$.

When the charge at $A$ is replaced by $-q$, the electric field at $O$ due to this new charge is $-\vec{E}_A$. The net electric field at $O$ is $\vec{E}_{net, 2} = \vec{E}_B + \vec{E}_C + \vec{E}_D + \vec{E}_E + \vec{E}_{-A} = -\vec{E}_A - \vec{E}_A = -2\vec{E}_A$. The magnitude is $|\vec{E}_{net, 2}| = 2E$.

The ratio of the magnitudes of the electric fields is $\dfrac{|\vec{E}_{net, 1}|}{|\vec{E}_{net, 2}|} = \dfrac{E}{2E} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: 1 : 2

22849.subject: Physics
22849.text: Two charged spheres of $-20 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $60 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are kept at a certain distance. They are touched and kept again at the same distance. What is the ratio of force experienced before and after?
22849.sol:
Let the charges on the two spheres be $q_1 = -20 \mu C$ and $q_2 = 60 \mu C$. Let the distance between them be $r$.

The electrostatic force before touching is given by Coulomb's law:
$F_1 = k \dfrac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2} = k \dfrac{|(-20)(60)|}{r^2} = k \dfrac{1200}{r^2}$

When the spheres are touched, the total charge is redistributed equally between the two identical spheres. The new charge on each sphere is:
$q' = \dfrac{q_1 + q_2}{2} = \dfrac{-20 + 60}{2} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20 \mu C$

The electrostatic force after touching is:
$F_2 = k \dfrac{|q' q'|}{r^2} = k \dfrac{|(20)(20)|}{r^2} = k \dfrac{400}{r^2}$

The ratio of the force before to the force after is:
$\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \dfrac{k \dfrac{1200}{r^2}}{k \dfrac{400}{r^2}} = \dfrac{1200}{400} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

Thus, the ratio is $3 : 1$.

Answer: 3 : 1

24322.subject: Physics
24322.text: An exotic spherical jellyfish has a bulk modulus $B$. Close to the surface of the sea (depth $d=0$), its radius is $R$. When it dives to a depth $d$ ($d \gg R$), its radius is reduced by $\Delta R > 0$. Given the density of the incompressible sea water $\rho$, and the uniform acceleration due to gravity $g$ such that $\rho g d \ll B$, what is $\dfrac{\Delta R}{R}$?
24322.sol:
The change in pressure at a depth $d$ is given by $\Delta P = \rho g d$.

The bulk modulus $B$ is defined as the ratio of volumetric stress to volumetric strain:

$B = -\dfrac{\Delta P}{\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = -\dfrac{\rho g d}{B}$

The new volume $V'$ of the jellyfish at depth $d$ is:

$V' = V + \Delta V = V \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)

Since the jellyfish is spherical, its volume is proportional to the cube of its radius (V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi$ R^3$). The new radius is $R - $\Delta$ R$, so the ratio of the new volume to the initial volume is:

\dfrac{V'}{V} = \left(\dfrac{R - \Delta R}{R}\right)^3 = \left(1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R}\right)^3$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{V'}{V}$:

$\left(1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R}\right)^3 = 1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}

Taking the cube root on both sides:

1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}

\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} =1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}

Answer: \left[1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}\right]$

30731.subject: Chemistry
30731.text:
Arrange the following resultant mixtures in increasing order of their pH values
A. $10$ mL $0.2$ M Ca(OH)$_2$ + $25$ mL $0.1$ M HCl
B. $10$ mL $0.01$ M H$_2$SO$_4$ + $10$ mL $0.01$ M Ca(OH)$_2$
C. $10$ mL $0.1$ M H$_2$SO$_4$ + $10$ mL $0.1$ M KOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30731.sol:
For mixture A:
Millimoles of OH$^{-}$ = $10 \times 0.2 \times 2 = 4$
Millimoles of H$^{+}$ = $25 \times 0.1 \times 1 = 2.5$
Remaining OH$^{-}$ = $4 - 2.5 = 1.5$ mmol
The solution is basic, so pH $> 7$.

For mixture B:
Millimoles of H$^{+}$ = $10 \times 0.01 \times 2 = 0.2$
Millimoles of OH$^{-}$ = $10 \times 0.01 \times 2 = 0.2$
The solution is completely neutralized, so pH $= 7$.

For mixture C:
Millimoles of H$^{+}$ = $10 \times 0.1 \times 2 = 2$
Millimoles of OH$^{-}$ = $10 \times 0.1 \times 1 = 1$
Remaining H$^{+}$ = $2 - 1 = 1$ mmol
The solution is acidic, so pH $< 7$.

Therefore, the increasing order of pH values is C $<$ B $<$ A.

Answer: $C < B < A$

$\dfrac{{W}_{0}}{eV}$ $2 . 42$ $2 . 3$ $2 . 25$ $3 . 7$ $4 . 8$ $4 . 3$

32234.sol:
The minimum amount of energy necessary to start the emission of electrons from a metal's surface is known as its work function. The work function is the minimum amount of energy required to remove an electron from a metal's surface to infinity.

Energy of incident photon $= \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

$= 3 . 1eV$

If radiation energy is greater than work function of metal, then metal show photo electric effect.

$∴ Li, Na$ and $K$ will show photoelectric effect.

32836.subject: Mathematics
32836.text:
Let $f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $\left(x{\log}_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$ with $f\left(2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} and f\left(4\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Consider the following two statements:

(A) $f\left(x\right) \le 1, \text{for all}x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

(B) $f\left(x\right)$ \ge 1 / 8, $\text{for all}x \in \left[2, 4\right]

Then,

$
options: Neither statement $( A )$ nor statement $( B )$ is true
Both the statements $( A )$and $( B )$are true
32836.sol:
Given,

Domain and range of function,

$f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$

$\left(x{\log}_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$⇒ \left(x{\log}_{e}x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}f\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) + xf\left(x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({\log}_{e}x\right) \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right)\right] \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right)\right] \ge \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right) - x\right] \ge 0$

Hence, $h ( x ) = x\left(lnx\right)f\left(x\right) - x$ is a increasing function,

$∴ h ( x ) \ge h ( 2 ) , x \in [ 2, 4 ]$

$⇒ xlnx \times f\left(x\right) - x \ge 2ln2 \times f\left(2\right) - 2$

$⇒ xlnxf ( x ) - x \ge ln2 - 2$

Similarly, $h\left(x\right) \le h\left(4\right)$

$⇒ xlnxf\left(x\right) - x \le ln4 - 4$

So, $\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \le f ( x ) \le \dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx}$

Now for $x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$\dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \le \dfrac{ln4 - 4}{2ln2} + \dfrac{1}{ln2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{ln2} < 1$

$⇒ f \left(x\right)$ \le 1$\text{for}x \in \left[2, 4\right]

Now$ for x \in $\left[2, 4\right]$

$\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx}$ \ge $\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4ln2}$ > $\dfrac{1}{8}

Hence, $f ( x ) \ge $\dfrac{1}{8}

Hence both A$ & $B$ are correct.
Note this question was bonus in Jee Main 2023 April session, as LMVT on $f ( x ) \cdot xlnx$ can't be satisfied.

Hence, no such $f ( x )$ exist.

33281.subject: Mathematics
33281.text: The number of elements in the set $S = \left\{(r, k) : k \in \mathbb{Z} \text{ and } {}^{36}C_{r+1} = \dfrac{6\left({}^{35}C_r\right)}{(k^2 - 3)}\right\}$, is :
33281.sol:
Given equation:

$^{36}C_{r+1} = \dfrac{6 \left(^{35}C_r\right)}{k^2 - 3}$

Using the property $^{n}C_r = \dfrac{n}{r} {}^{n-1}C_{r-1}$, we can write:

$^{36}C_{r+1} = \dfrac{36}{r+1} {}^{35}C_r$

Substituting this into the given equation:

$\dfrac{36}{r+1} {}^{35}C_r = \dfrac{6}{k^2 - 3} {}^{35}C_r$

For $^{35}C_r$ to be defined, $r$ must be an integer such that $0 \le r \le 35$. Thus, $^{35}C_r \neq 0$. Dividing both sides by $^{35}C_r$:

$\dfrac{36}{r+1} = \dfrac{6}{k^2 - 3}$

$\dfrac{6}{r+1} = \dfrac{1}{k^2 - 3}$

$k^2 - 3 = \dfrac{r+1}{6}$

$k^2 = 3 + \dfrac{r+1}{6}$

For $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, $k^2$ must be a perfect square integer. This requires $r+1$ to be a multiple of $6$.

Since $0 \le r \le 35$, we have $1 \le r+1 \le 36$.

Let $r+1 = 6m$, where $m \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$.

Then $k^2 = 3 + m$.

Checking the possible values of $m$ for which $k^2$ is a perfect square:

For $m = 1$, $k^2 = 4 \Rightarrow k = \pm 2$. (Here $r+1 = 6 \Rightarrow r = 5$)

For $m = 2$, $k^2 = 5$ (not a perfect square).

For $m = 3$, $k^2 = 6$ (not a perfect square).

For $m = 4$, $k^2 = 7$ (not a perfect square).

For $m = 5$, $k^2 = 8$ (not a perfect square).

For $m = 6$, $k^2 = 9 \Rightarrow k = \pm 3$. (Here $r+1 = 36 \Rightarrow r = 35$)

The possible pairs $(r, k)$ are $(5, 2)$, $(5, -2)$, $(35, 3)$, and $(35, -3)$.

Therefore, the number of elements in the set $S$ is $4$.

Answer: $4$

To find the coefficient of term independent of $x$ in given expression, first let's find constant term and coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}$ in the expansion of ${\left(2{x}^{2} - \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{6}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{\left(2{x}^{2}\right)}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{2}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{r} \times {x}^{12 - 4r}$
For constant term: $r = 3$ , hence constant term = ${}^{6}{C}_{3}{2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times {x}^{0}$
For coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}: r = 5$ , hence coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}{=}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1}{\left(- 3\right)}^{5} \times {x}^{- 8}$
Given expression can be written as
$\left(\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{{x}^{8}}{81}\right)\left({}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times {x}^{0} + \ldots + {}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{5} \times {x}^{- 8} + \ldots\right)$
Hence, coefficient of term independent of $x$
$= \dfrac{1}{60}{\times}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3}{\left(- 3\right)}^{3} - \dfrac{1}{81}{\times}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{5}$
$= - 72 + 36 = - 36$

37494.text: Let the mean and the variance of seven observations $2, 4, \alpha, 8, \beta, 12, 14$, $\alpha < \beta$, be $8$ and $16$ respectively. Then the quadratic equation whose roots are $3\alpha + 2$ and $2\beta + 1$ is :
37494.sol:
Given the mean of the seven observations is $8$:

$\dfrac{2 + 4 + \alpha + 8 + \beta + 12 + 14}{7} = 8$

$\dfrac{40 + \alpha + \beta}{7} = 8$

$\alpha + \beta = 16$

Given the variance of the observations is $16$:

$\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n} - (\text{Mean})^2 = 16$

$\dfrac{2^2 + 4^2 + \alpha^2 + 8^2 + \beta^2 + 12^2 + 14^2}{7} - 8^2 = 16$

$\dfrac{4 + 16 + \alpha^2 + 64 + \beta^2 + 144 + 196}{7} - 64 = 16$

$\dfrac{424 + \alpha^2 + \beta^2}{7} = 80$

$424 + \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 560$

$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 136$

Using the identity $(\alpha + \beta)^2 = \alpha^2 + \beta^2 + 2\alpha\beta$:

$16^2 = 136 + 2\alpha\beta$

$256 = 136 + 2\alpha\beta$

$2\alpha\beta = 120 \Rightarrow \alpha\beta = 60$

Solving for $\alpha$ and $\beta$, they are the roots of the equation $t^2 - 16t + 60 = 0$, which are $6$ and $10$.

Since $\alpha < \beta$, we have $\alpha = 6$ and $\beta = 10$.

The roots of the required quadratic equation are $3\alpha + 2$ and $2\beta + 1$:

$3\alpha + 2 = 3(6) + 2 = 20$

$2\beta + 1 = 2(10) + 1 = 21$

Sum of the roots $= 20 + 21 = 41$

Product of the roots $= 20 \times 21 = 420$

37663.subject: Mathematics
37663.text: Let the vertex $A$ of a triangle $ABC$ be $(1, 2)$, and the mid-point of the side $AB$ be $(5, -1)$. If the centroid of this triangle is $(3, 4)$ and its circumcenter is $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $21(\alpha + \beta)$ is equal to:
37663.sol:
Let the coordinates of vertex $B$ be $(x_1, y_1)$ and vertex $C$ be $(x_2, y_2)$.

Since the mid-point of $AB$ is $(5, -1)$, we have:
$\dfrac{1 + x_1}{2} = 5 \Rightarrow x_1 = 9$
$\dfrac{2 + y_1}{2} = -1 \Rightarrow y_1 = -4$
Thus, $B \equiv (9, -4)$.

Given the centroid of $\triangle ABC$ is $(3, 4)$, we get:
$\dfrac{1 + 9 + x_2}{3} = 3 \Rightarrow x_2 = -1$
$\dfrac{2 - 4 + y_2}{3} = 4 \Rightarrow y_2 = 14$
Thus, $C \equiv (-1, 14)$.

The circumcenter $(\alpha, \beta)$ is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of the triangle.

For side $AB$, the mid-point is $(5, -1)$ and the slope is $\dfrac{-4 - 2}{9 - 1} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$.
The slope of its perpendicular bisector is $\dfrac{4}{3}$.
Equation of the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is:
$y - (-1) = \dfrac{4}{3}(x - 5) \Rightarrow 4x - 3y = 23$

For side $AC$, the mid-point is $\left(\dfrac{1 - 1}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 14}{2}\right) = (0, 8)$ and the slope is $\dfrac{14 - 2}{-1 - 1} = -6$.
The slope of its perpendicular bisector is $\dfrac{1}{6}$.
Equation of the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ is:
$y - 8 = \dfrac{1}{6}(x - 0) \Rightarrow x - 6y = -48$

Solving the equations $4x - 3y = 23$ and $x - 6y = -48$:
Multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives $8x - 6y = 46$.
Subtracting the second equation from this gives:
$7x = 94 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{94}{7}$
Substituting $x$ into the second equation:
$\dfrac{94}{7} - 6y = -48 \Rightarrow 6y = \dfrac{430}{7} \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{215}{21}$

Therefore, the circumcenter is $(\alpha, \beta) = \left(\dfrac{94}{7}, \dfrac{215}{21}\right)$.

Finally, calculating $21(\alpha + \beta)$:
$21(\alpha + \beta) = 21\left(\dfrac{94}{7} + \dfrac{215}{21}\right) = 3(94) + 215 = 282 + 215 = 497$.

Answer: $497$

38071.text: The plane passing through the line $L: lx - y + 3\left(1 - l\right)$ $z = 1, x + 2y - z = 2$ and perpendicular to the plane $3x + 2y + z = 6$ is $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$. If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the line $L$ and the $y$-axis, then $415\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to ______.
38071.sol:
Given the plane passing through the line ${L}_{1}: lx - y + 3\left(1 - l\right)z = 1$, ${L}_{2}: x + 2y - z = 2$ and perpendicular to the plane $3x + 2y + z = 6$ is $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$,

So direction ratio of line ${L}_{1}$ will be $\overset{\to}{n}1 = l\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\left(1 - l\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And ${L}_{2}$ will be $\overset{\to}{n}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now direction ratio of line $= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ l & - 1 & 3\left(1 - l\right) \\ 1 & 2 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(6l - 5\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - 2l\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2l + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Also plane $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$ will contain the line $\left(6l - 5\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - 2l\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2l + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

So, normal of $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$ will be perpendicular to the line

$⇒ 3\left(6l - 5\right) + \left(3 - 2l\right)\left(- 8\right) + 7\left(2l + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, direction ratio of line $\left(- 1, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$

Now finding angle with $y$ axis

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3}}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{25}{9} + \dfrac{49}{9}}}$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{83}}$

So, $415\cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{25}{83} \times 415 = 125$

42847.text: Light ray incident along a vector $\vec{AO}$ $(\vec{AO} = 2\hat{i}-3\hat{j})$ emerges out along vector $\vec{OB}$ $(\vec{OB} = C\hat{i}-4\hat{j})$ as shown in the figure below. The value of $C$ is ________.
42847.sol:
From the given figure, the interface is horizontal and the normal is along the y-axis.

The incident ray is along the vector $\vec{AO} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$.
The angle of incidence $\alpha$ is the angle between the incident ray and the normal.
$\sin \alpha = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2^2 + (-3)^2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}$

The refracted ray is along the vector $\vec{OB} = C\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}$.
The angle of refraction $\beta$ is the angle between the refracted ray and the normal.
$\sin \beta = \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2 + (-4)^2}} = \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2 + 16}}$

Applying Snell's law at the interface:
$\mu_1 \sin \alpha = \mu_2 \sin \beta$
$1 \times \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}} = 1.5 \times \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2 + 16}}$
$\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}} = \dfrac{3}{2} \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2 + 16}}$

Squaring both sides:
$\dfrac{4}{13} = \dfrac{9}{4} \left( \dfrac{C^2}{C^2 + 16} \right)$
$16(C^2 + 16) = 117 C^2$
$16 C^2 + 256 = 117 C^2$
$101 C^2 = 256$
$C^2 = \dfrac{256}{101}$
$C = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{101}} \approx 1.592$

Approximating $\sqrt{101} \approx 10$, we get $C \approx 1.6$.

Answer: $1.6$

43169.text: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of $M$. Two blocks of mass of $M$ and $m$ are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is $\_\_\_\_$ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
43169.sol:
The pulley consists of a rim (mass $M$) and two rods (each mass $M$) forming a diameter structure.
The moment of inertia is: $I = I_{rim} + I_{rods} = MR^2 + 2 \times \frac{MR^2}{3} = \frac{5MR^2}{3}$.
For the Atwood pulley system, applying Newton's second law:
Mass $m$ (upward): $T_1 = m(g-a)$
Mass $M$ (downward): $T_2 = M(g+a)$
Pulley rotation: $T_2 R - T_1 R = I\alpha = \frac{5MR^2}{3} \cdot \frac{a}{R}$
Thus: $T_2 - T_1 = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
Substituting: $M(g+a) - m(g-a) = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
$(M-m)g + (M+m)a = \frac{5Ma}{3}$

48283.text: Henry's law constant for the solubility of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ gas in water at $298 \mathrm{ K}$ is $1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{ atm}$. The mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ in air is $0.8$. Mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\left(\chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}\right)=0.8$
Hence, partial pressure of nitrogen,
$\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} &=p_{\text{total }} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} \\
&=0.8 \times 5 \mathrm{ atm} \\
&=4 \mathrm{ atm}
\end{aligned}$
According to Henry's law,
$\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} &=K_{\mathrm{H}} \chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} \\
4 &=10^{5} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} \\
\chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} &=4 \times 10^{-5}
\end{aligned}$
We know that,
$\begin{aligned}
\chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} &=\frac{n_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}}{n_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}+n_{\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}}} \\
\Rightarrow \quad 4 \times 10^{-5} &=\frac{n_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}}{10} \quad\left(\because n_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}< <  <  n_{\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \quad n_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} &=4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ moles }
\end{aligned}$
Thus, the number of moles of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ from air dissolved in 10 moles of water at $295 \mathrm{ K}  and 5 atm pressure is $4 \times 10^{-4}$.$

49086.text: If the curves $2 x=y^{2}$ and $2 x y=K$ intersect perpendicularly, then the value of $K^{2}$ is
49086.sol:
Given curves are
$2 x=y^{2}...(i)
and 2 x y=K...(ii)$
On solving both Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$x=\frac{K^{2 / 3}}{2} \text{$ and $} y=K^{1 / 3}\therefore$ Intersecting point of both curves is $\left(\frac{K^{2 / 3}}{2}, K^{1 / 3}\right)$
Now differentiate Eq. (i) w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
2 &=2 y \frac{d y}{d x} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{1}{y}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Slope of tangent at $\left(\frac{K^{2 / 3}}{2}, K^{1 / 3}\right)=\frac{1}{K^{1 / 3}}$
And differentiate Eq. (ii) w.r.t. $x$, we get
$2\left(x \frac{d y}{d x}+y\right)=0 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-y}{x}\therefore$ Slope of tangent at $\left(\frac{K^{2 / 3}}{2}, K^{1 / 3}\right)=\frac{-K^{1 / 3}}{K^{2 / 3} / 2}=-2 K^{-1 / 3}$
Since, both curves intersect perpendicularly
$\begin{aligned}
&\therefore \quad \frac{1}{K^{1 / 3}} \times\left(-2 K^{-1 / 3}\right)=-1 \\
&\Rightarrow \quad-2 K^{-2 / 3}=-1 \Rightarrow K^{2 / 3}=2 \Rightarrow K^{2}=8
\end{aligned}$

49535.text: The three points $A(2, 4, 3), B(4, a, 9)$ and $C(10, -1, 7)$ form a right-angled triangle with $\angle B = 90^{}^{\circ}$, then the value of "a" is
49535.sol:
The given points are $A(2, 4, 3)$, $B(4, a, 9)$, and $C(10, -1, 7)$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $AB$ are $(2 - 4, 4 - a, 3 - 9) = (-2, 4 - a, -6)$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $BC$ are $(10 - 4, -1 - a, 7 - 9) = (6, -1 - a, -2)$.

Since $\angle B = 90^{}^{\circ}$, the line segments $AB$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the dot product of their direction vectors is zero.

$(-2)(6) + (4 - a)(-1 - a) + (-6)(-2) = 0$

$-12 - (4 - a)(1 + a) + 12 = 0$

$(a - 4)(a + 1) = 0$

$a = 4$ or $a = -1$

Answer: $-1$ or $4$

\text{ Variance } & =\frac{\Sigma n^2}{n}-\left(\frac{\Sigma n}{n}\right)^2 \\
& =\frac{n(n+1)(2 n-1)}{6 n}-\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2 n}\right)^2 \\
& =(n+1)\left[\frac{2 n-1}{6}-\frac{(n+1)}{4}\right] \\
& =\frac{(n+1)}{12}[4 n-2-3 n-3] \\
& =\frac{(n+1)}{12} \times(n-5)
\end{aligned}$

54872.text: Which of the following on reaction with Grignards reagent followed by hydrolysis forms tertiary alcohol?
54872.sol:
Grignard reagents react with carbonyl compounds followed by hydrolysis to yield alcohols, with the alcohol type determined by the carbonyl substrate.
Methanal produces primary alcohols:
\($\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrm{HCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{ 1. Ether, 2. } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}+} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CH}}_{2}-$\mathrm{OH}$\)
Aldehydes other than methanal yield secondary alcohols:

Ketones form tertiary alcohols:
\(\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrm{R}^{\prime}2  \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\text{ 1. Ether, 2. } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}+} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CR}$}_{2}^{\prime}-$\mathrm{OH}$\)
Among the options, propanone is a ketone and thus produces a tertiary alcohol.

56282.text: Which of the following statement about enzyme is correct ?
options: They alter the equilibrium constant of reactions
They increase the activation energy of reactions
They are specific in their action
They are consumed in the reaction
56282.sol:
Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up the rate of biochemical reactions without being consumed in the process.

They do not alter the equilibrium constant of a reaction; they only help attain equilibrium faster.

They work by lowering the activation energy of the reaction, not increasing it.

Enzymes are highly specific in their action, meaning each enzyme typically catalyzes only one specific reaction or acts on a specific substrate.

Thus, the statement that they are specific in their action is correct.

Answer: They are specific in their action

56807.subject: Chemistry
56807.text: If standard reduction potential of four electrodes A, B, C, D are $+2.5\,\text{V}, +3.0\,\text{V}, -2.0\,\text{V}$ and $-1.5\,\text{V}$ respectively. When is the standard emf of cell maximum?
56807.sol:
The standard emf of a cell is given by $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{anode}}$.

To obtain the maximum standard emf, the cathode must have the highest standard reduction potential and the anode must have the lowest standard reduction potential.

Given standard reduction potentials are:
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{A}} = +2.5\text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{B}} = +3.0\text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{C}} = -2.0\text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{D}} = -1.5\text{ V}$

The highest reduction potential is for electrode B ($+3.0\text{ V}$), so B should act as the cathode.

The lowest reduction potential is for electrode C ($-2.0\text{ V}$), so C should act as the anode.

Maximum $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = 3.0 - (-2.0) = 5.0\text{ V}$.

Thus, 'C' is the anode and 'B' is the cathode.

Answer: 'C' is anode and 'B' is cathode

57133.text: Which from following structures represents 1,3 butadiene ?
57133.sol:
The IUPAC name 1,3-butadiene corresponds to a four-carbon chain with two double bonds located at the 1st and 3rd carbon atoms.

The chemical formula is $CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2$.

Let us analyze the given bond-line structures:
1. The first structure has a five-carbon chain with one double bond at the second position, representing pent-2-ene.
2. The second structure has a four-carbon chain with double bonds at the first and third positions, representing 1,3-butadiene.
3. The third structure has a four-carbon chain with a triple bond at the first position, representing but-1-yne.
4. The fourth structure has a three-carbon chain with a triple bond, representing propyne.

Therefore, the second structure correctly represents 1,3-butadiene.

Answer:

58007.text: The solubility product of AgBr is $4.9 \times 10^{-13}$ at a certain temperature. Calculate the solubility.
58007.sol:
The dissolution equilibrium for silver bromide is: $\mathrm{AgBr(s) \rightleftharpoons Ag^+(aq) + Br^-(aq)}$

For this equilibrium, the solubility product expression gives $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ag^+}][\mathrm{Br^-}]$. If $s$ represents the molar solubility, then $[\mathrm{Ag^+}] = s$ and $[\mathrm{Br^-}] = s$, yielding $K_{sp} = s^2$.

Given $K_{sp} = 4.9 \times 10^{-13}$, we solve $s^2 = 4.9 \times 10^{-13}$. Converting to $49 \times 10^{-14}$ and taking square roots:

$s = \sqrt{49 \times 10^{-14}} = 7 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{mol dm^{-3}}$

This value corresponds to option C among the given choices.

Answer: C

58232.subject: Chemistry
58232.text: Which of the following xenon compound has chlorine pentafluoride like structure?
58232.sol:
Xenon compounds share structural similarities with interhalogens when their molecular geometries match. Chlorine pentafluoride (ClF_5$) has a square pyramidal geometry arising from an octahedral electron domain with one lone pair and five bonding pairs.

Among xenon compounds, XeF_4$ is square planar, XeF_6$ is distorted octahedral, and XeO_3$ is pyramidal. XeOF_4$ features xenon bonded to four fluorine atoms and one oxygen atom via a double bond, yielding five bonding domains and one lone pair. This $sp^3d^2$ hybridized configuration results in a square pyramidal geometry identical to $ClF_5$.

The xenon compound with structure analogous to $ClF_5$ is \boxed{\text{D}}$.

59916.subject: Chemistry
59916.text: Calculate $\Delta S_{\text{total }}$ for a certain reaction if $\Delta H=-150 \mathrm{ kJ}  and $\Delta S=32 $\mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ at 300 K.
59916.sol:
The total entropy change for a reaction combines system and surroundings contributions: $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$.

The entropy change of the surroundings follows from the enthalpy change at constant temperature: $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{\Delta H}{T}$.

Given $\Delta H = -150 \times 10^3\ \mathrm{J}$ and $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, substitution yields $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{-150 \times 10^3}{300} = 500\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$.

Adding the system entropy change $\Delta S_{\text{system}} = 32\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ gives $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 32 + 500 = 532\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$.

The value $532\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ corresponds to option B.

60289.subject: Mathematics
60289.text: A population $\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{t})$ of 1000 bacteria introduced into a nutrient medium grows according to the relation $\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{t})=1000+\frac{1000 \mathrm{t}}{100+\mathrm{t}^2}$. The maximum size of this bacterial population is
60289.sol:
Maximum bacterial population

To determine the maximum population size, maximize the function $p(t) = 1000 + \frac{1000t}{100+t^2}$.

The maximum of $p(t)$ occurs at the same $t$ as the maximum of $\frac{1000t}{100+t^2}$, since 1000 is constant. Differentiate this function:

$f'(t) = \frac{1000(100+t^2) - 1000t(2t)}{(100+t^2)^2} = \frac{100000 - 1000t^2}{(100+t^2)^2}$

Set the derivative to zero to find critical points. Only $t = 10$ is physically meaningful in the domain $t \geq 0$.

The population at $t = 10$ is $p(10) = 1000 + \frac{1000 \times 10}{100+100} = 1000 + 50 = 1050$.

Since $f'(t) > 0$ for $t < 10$ and $f'(t) < 0$ for $t > 10$, this is a maximum. The population approaches 1000 as $t \to 0$ and $t \to \infty$, confirming 1050 is the global maximum.

$\boxed{1050}$

60681.subject: Mathematics
60681.text: If $x$, y, z are the sides of a right angled triangle, where z is the largest side, then $\dfrac{1}{\log_{x+z} y} + \dfrac{1}{\log_{z-x} y} =$
60681.sol:
Since $x, y, z$ are the sides of a right-angled triangle and $z$ is the largest side, $z$ is the hypotenuse.

By Pythagoras theorem, $x^2 + y^2 = z^2$, which gives $y^2 = z^2 - x^2$.

The given expression is $\dfrac{1}{\log_{x+z} y} + \dfrac{1}{\log_{z-x} y}$.

Using the property $\dfrac{1}{\log_a b} = \log_b a$, the expression can be written as:

$\log_y (x+z) + \log_y (z-x)$

Using the property $\log_a m + \log_a n = \log_a (mn)$, we get:

$\log_y ((x+z)(z-x))$

$\Rightarrow \log_y (z^2 - x^2)$

Substituting $z^2 - x^2 = y^2$, we get:

$\log_y (y^2) = 2 \log_y y = 2$

Answer: $2$

61284.text: The rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of a persons existing assets at that moment. If his assets at the beginning are 10000 and they dwindle down to 5625 in 2 years, then the person will be bankrupt in
61284.sol:
Let $A$ be the assets at time $t$. The rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of the existing assets.

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -k\sqrt{A}$

Separating the variables and integrating:

$\int \dfrac{dA}{\sqrt{A}} = \int -k dt$

$2\sqrt{A} = -kt + C$

At $t = 0$, $A = 10000$

$2\sqrt{10000} = -k(0) + C \Rightarrow C = 200$

At $t = 2$ years, $A = 5625$

$2\sqrt{5625} = -k(2) + 200$

$2(75) = -2k + 200$

$150 = -2k + 200 \Rightarrow 2k = 50 \Rightarrow k = 25$

The equation for the assets at time $t$ becomes:

$2\sqrt{A} = -25t + 200$

For the person to be bankrupt, the assets $A$ must be $0$.

$2\sqrt{0} = -25t + 200$

$25t = 200 \Rightarrow t = 8$ years

Answer: 8 years

63560.text: Consider a game of tossing a six sided fair die. If the face that comes up is $6$, the player wins Rs. $36$ and he loses Rs. $k^2$, where $k$ is the face that comes up $k = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$, then the expected winning amount in this game in Rs. is...
63560.sol:
Let $X$ be the random variable representing the winning amount.

The possible values of $X$ corresponding to the outcomes $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ on the die are $-1^2, -2^2, -3^2, -4^2, -5^2, 36$ respectively, which simplifies to $-1, -4, -9, -16, -25, 36$.

Since the die is fair, the probability of each outcome is $\dfrac{1}{6}$.

The expected winning amount is given by $E(X) = \sum x_i P(x_i)$.

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-1) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-4) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-9) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-16) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-25) + \dfrac{1}{6}(36)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-1 - 4 - 9 - 16 - 25 + 36)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-55 + 36)$

$E(X) = -\dfrac{19}{6}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{19}{6}$

63585.text: If A and B are two events such that $P(A) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $P(A \mid B) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, then $P(A' \cup B) + P(A \cup B') = $

Given $P(A) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $P(A \mid B) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$P(A \cap B) = P(A \mid B) P(B) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$P(A' \cup B) = 1 - P(A \cap B') = 1 - (P(A) - P(A \cap B))$

$P(A' \cup B) = 1 - \left(\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$P(A \cup B') = 1 - P(A' \cap B) = 1 - (P(B) - P(A \cap B))$

$P(A \cup B') = 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{6}$

$P(A' \cup B) + P(A \cup B') = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{9}{6} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

64457.sol:
The projection of the vector $\vec{PQ}$ onto a line with direction cosines $(l, m, n)$ is given by the absolute value of $A_x l + A_y m + A_z n$.

First, compute $\vec{PQ} = (3-2, 2-(-1), -1-0) = (1, 3, -1)$.

Given direction ratios $(1,2,2)$, the magnitude is $\sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = 3$. Thus, the direction cosines are $\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{2}{3}\right)$.

The projection evaluates to $\left|1 \cdot \frac{1}{3} + 3 \cdot \frac{2}{3} + (-1) \cdot \frac{2}{3}\right| = \left|\frac{1}{3} + \frac{6}{3} - \frac{2}{3}\right| = \frac{5}{3}$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

66301.text:
In the following network,
$I_1 = -0.4\,\text{A}$ , $I_4 = 1\,\text{A}$ , $I_5 = 0.4\,\text{A}$
The values of $I_2$, $I_3$ and $I_6$ are respectively
66301.sol:
Let the nodes of the network be identified by their positions.

Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) at the top-left node:
The current entering the node is $I_5$ and the current leaving is $I_6$.
$I_6 = I_5$
Given $I_5 = 0.4\,\text{A}$, we get $I_6 = 0.4\,\text{A}$.

Applying KCL at the bottom-left node:
The currents entering the node are $I_3$ and $I_4$, and the current leaving is $I_5$.
$I_3 + I_4 = I_5$
Substituting the given values $I_4 = 1\,\text{A}$ and $I_5 = 0.4\,\text{A}$:
$I_3 + 1 = 0.4$
$I_3 = -0.6\,\text{A}$

Applying KCL at the bottom-right node:
The currents entering the node are $I_1$ and $I_2$, and the current leaving is $I_4$.
$I_1 + I_2 = I_4$
Substituting the given values $I_1 = -0.4\,\text{A}$ and $I_4 = 1\,\text{A}$:
$-0.4 + I_2 = 1$
$I_2 = 1.4\,\text{A}$

Therefore, the values of $I_2$, $I_3$, and $I_6$ are respectively $1.4\,\text{A}$, $-0.6\,\text{A}$, and $0.4\,\text{A}$.

Answer: $1.4\,\text{A}$ , $-0.6\,\text{A}$ , $0.4\,\text{A}$

Simplifying: $L = \frac{108}{7.2} \times 10^{-3} = 15 \times 10^{-3} \text{m}$.

Convert to centimeters: $15 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 = 1.5 \text{cm}$.

The inner circumference is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

69953.subject: Physics
69953.text: During thermodynamic process, the increase in internal energy of a system is equal to the work done on the system. Which process does the system undergo?
69953.sol:
The First Law of Thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy ΔU equals the heat added to the system Q plus the work done on the system W: $\Delta U = Q + W$.

Given that ΔU = W, substitution yields $W = Q + W$, which simplifies to $Q = 0$. A process with no heat exchange (Q = 0) is adiabatic.

Other processes are incompatible: isothermal implies $\Delta U = 0$ but not necessarily W = 0; isochoric gives W = 0 but not necessarily $\Delta U = 0$; isobaric has no inherent constraint linking ΔU and W.

The process is adiabatic, corresponding to option B.

70462.subject: Physics
70462.text: What is the effect of humidity on sound waves when humidity increases?
options: Speed of sound waves is more.
Speed of sound waves is less.
Speed of sound waves remains same.
Speed of sound waves becomes zero.
70462.sol:
The speed of sound in a gas is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma R T}{M}}$, where $M$ is the molar mass of the gas.

Dry air consists mainly of nitrogen ($N_2$, molar mass $28$ g/mol) and oxygen ($O_2$, molar mass $32$ g/mol), giving an average molar mass of approximately $28.97$ g/mol.

Water vapor ($H_2O$) has a molar mass of $18$ g/mol. When humidity increases, water vapor displaces heavier nitrogen and oxygen molecules, which decreases the average molar mass $M$ of the air.

Since the speed of sound is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass ($v \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$), a decrease in molar mass leads to an increase in the speed of sound.

Thus, when humidity increases, the speed of sound waves is more.

Answer: Speed of sound waves is more.

70463.subject: Physics
70463.text: A person observes two moving trains. First reaching the station and another leaves the station with equal speed of $30 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. If both trains emit sounds of frequency 300 Hz , difference of frequencies heard by the person will be (speed of sound in air $=330 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
70463.sol:
The Doppler effect governs the frequency shift for a moving source relative to a stationary observer. For a source approaching the observer, the observed frequency is $f_1 = f_0 \frac{v}{v - v_s}$, while for a receding source, it is $f_2 = f_0 \frac{v}{v + v_s}$, where $f_0 = 300 \, \text{Hz}$, $v = 330 \, \text{m/s}$, and $v_s = 30 \, \text{m/s}$.

For the approaching train: $f_1 = 300 \times \frac{330}{330 - 30} = 300 \times \frac{330}{300} = 330 \, \text{Hz}$.

For the receding train: $f_2 = 300 \times \frac{330}{330 + 30} = 300 \times \frac{330}{360} = 275 \, \text{Hz}$.

The difference in frequencies is $|f_1 - f_2| = |330 - 275| = 55 \, \text{Hz}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{55}$

70477.text: An air column is of length 17 cm. The ratio of frequencies of $5^{\text{th }}$ overtone if the air column is closed at one end to that open at both ends is (velocity of sound in air $=340 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}  )$
70477.sol:
Key Concepts
For a closed organ pipe, only odd harmonics exist with frequencies $f_n = (2n-1)\frac{v}{4L}$ where $n=1,2,3,\dots$; the $k^\text{th}$ overtone corresponds to $n = k+1$. For an open organ pipe, all harmonics are present with frequencies $f_n = n\frac{v}{2L}$, where the $k^\text{th}$ overtone corresponds to $n = k+1$.

The fifth overtone in a closed pipe gives $n=6$, so $f_\text{closed} = (2\times6-1)\frac{v}{4L} = \frac{11v}{4L}$.

The fifth overtone in an open pipe gives $n=6$, so $f_\text{open} = 6\cdot\frac{v}{2L} = \frac{3v}{L}$.

The ratio is $\frac{f_\text{closed}}{f_\text{open}} = \frac{\frac{11v}{4L}}{\frac{3v}{L}} = \frac{11v}{4L} \cdot \frac{L}{3v} = \frac{11}{12}$, eliminating dependencies on length and velocity.

The answer is $\frac{11}{12}$.

70847.text: A pendulum bob has a speed $4 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ at its lowest position. The pendulum is 1 m long. When the length of the string makes an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the vertical, the speed of the bob at that position is (acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}=0 \cdot 5$ )
70847.sol:
The speed $v_2$ of the pendulum bob when the string makes an angle of $60^{}^{\circ}$ with the vertical can be found using conservation of mechanical energy, taking the lowest position as the reference for potential energy.

At the lowest position, the speed is $v_1 = 4 \, \text{m/s}$, so the total energy is $\frac{1}{2}mv_1^2 = 8m$.

At $\theta = 60^{}^{\circ}$, the bob is at a height $h = L(1 - \cos\theta) = 0.5 \, \text{m}$ above the reference level, giving a potential energy of $mgh = 5m$.

By conservation of energy, $\frac{1}{2}mv_1^2 = mgh + \frac{1}{2}mv_2^2$. Cancelling $m$ and multiplying by 2 yields $v_1^2 = 2gh + v_2^2$, so $v_2^2 = v_1^2 - 2gh = 16 - 10 = 6$.

The speed is therefore $v_2 = \sqrt{6} \, \text{m/s}$, corresponding to choice $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

71096.text: Lob fin fish __________ is considered living fossil.
71096.sol:
Coelacanth is a lobe-finned fish that was thought to be extinct but was discovered alive in 1938 in South Africa. It has remained largely unchanged for millions of years and is therefore considered a living fossil.

Cichlid fish are a diverse family of ray-finned fishes.

Seymouria is an extinct genus of amphibian-like tetrapods.

Ichthyosaurs are extinct marine reptiles.

71131.subject: Biology
71131.text: What is extreme over-indulgence in food among adolescents called?
71131.sol:
Bulimia is an eating disorder characterized by extreme over-indulgence in food (binge eating), often followed by purging to avoid weight gain.

Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by an abnormally low body weight and an intense fear of gaining weight, leading to severe food restriction.

Amnesia refers to the loss of memories, such as facts, information, and experiences.

Illusion is a distortion of the senses, which can reveal how the human brain normally organizes and interprets sensory stimulation.

Answer: Bulimia

71409.text: Which one of the following is NOT a draw back of intra-uterine devices (IUDs) for birth control?
71409.sol:
Intra-uterine devices (IUDs) are a popular and effective reversible method of contraception.

IUDs do not cause permanent infertility; normal fertility is restored promptly after the removal of the device.

Therefore, the statement that it leads to permanent infertility is incorrect and is not a drawback of IUDs.

71501.subject: Biology
71501.text: Dioecy in some plants can prevent ________.
71501.sol:
Dioecy is the condition in which male and female flowers are borne on different plants, meaning each individual plant is either male or female (e.g., papaya).

Since a single plant does not possess both male and female reproductive organs, self-pollination cannot occur. Therefore, this condition prevents both autogamy (pollination within the same flower) and geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant).

It promotes xenogamy (cross-pollination), which is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one plant to the stigma of a different plant.

Answer: autogamy

71939.subject: Chemistry
71939.text: An element has bcc structure with atomic radius 200 pm. Find the volume of unit cell.
71939.sol:
For a bcc unit cell, the relation between edge length $a$ and atomic radius $r$ is given by:

$\sqrt{3}a = 4r$

$a = \dfrac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}$

Substituting $r = 200 \text{ pm} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$:

$a = \dfrac{4 \times 2 \times 10^{-8}}{1.732} \approx 4.618 \times 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$

Volume of the unit cell, $V = a^3$

$V = (4.618 \times 10^{-8})^3 \approx 9.848 \times 10^{-23} \text{ cm}^3$

Answer: $9.848 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$

72239.subject: Physics
72239.text: If the pressure of the gas is kept constant, then the mean free path (\lambda$) of a gas varies with temperature (T$) according to relation
72239.sol:
The mean free path of a gas molecule is given by

$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 n}$

where $d$ is the diameter of the molecule and $n$ is the number of molecules per unit volume.

From the ideal gas equation, $P = n k_B T$, which gives $n = \dfrac{P}{k_B T}$.

Substituting this into the expression for mean free path, we get

$\lambda = \dfrac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P}$

For a given gas at constant pressure, $P$ is constant. Therefore,

$\lambda \propto T$

Answer: $\lambda \propto T$

72444.subject: Physics
72444.text:
In a single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction experiment, the first secondary minimum is observed at an angle of $30^{}^{\circ}$ for light of wavelength $\lambda$. If the same slit is now illuminated by light of the same wavelength, the angular position (\theta$) of the first secondary maximum is
(\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$).
72444.sol:
For a single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction, the condition for the $n$-th secondary minimum is given by:

$a \sin \theta = n\lambda$

For the first secondary minimum ($n=1$) at $\theta = 30^{}^{\circ}$:

$a \sin 30^{}^{\circ} = \lambda$

$a \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \lambda \Rightarrow a = 2\lambda$

The condition for the $n$-th secondary maximum is given by:

$a \sin \theta' = \left(n + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$

For the first secondary maximum ($n=1$):

$a \sin \theta' = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}$

Substituting $a = 2\lambda$ into the equation:

$(2\lambda) \sin \theta' = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}$

$\sin \theta' = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\theta' = \sin^{-1} \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)

Answer: \sin^{-1}(3/4)$

72473.subject: Physics
72473.text: Two uniform strings X and Y made of same material made to vibrate under same tension. If the second overtone of string X is equal to the third overtone of string Y and the radius of string X is thrice that of string Y. The ratio of length of string X to that of Y is
72473.sol:
The frequency of the $p$-th harmonic of a stretched string is given by $f = \dfrac{p}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$

The linear mass density is $\mu = \pi r^2 \rho$, where $r$ is the radius and $\rho$ is the density of the material.

Substituting $\mu$, we get $f = \dfrac{p}{2Lr} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi \rho}}$

For string X, the second overtone corresponds to the third harmonic, so $p_X = 3$.

For string Y, the third overtone corresponds to the fourth harmonic, so $p_Y = 4$.

Since both strings are made of the same material and are under the same tension, $\rho$ and $T$ are constant.

Given that the frequencies are equal ($f_X = f_Y$):

$\dfrac{3}{2L_X r_X} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi \rho}} = \dfrac{4}{2L_Y r_Y} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi \rho}}$

$\dfrac{3}{L_X r_X} = \dfrac{4}{L_Y r_Y}$

$\dfrac{L_X}{L_Y} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{r_Y}{r_X}$

It is given that the radius of string X is thrice that of string Y, so $r_X = 3r_Y$, which means $\dfrac{r_Y}{r_X} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

$\dfrac{L_X}{L_Y} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

The ratio of the length of string X to that of Y is $1 : 4$.

Answer: $1 : 4$

81395.subject: Chemistry
81395.text: During Lassaigne's test, the elements present in an organic compound are converted from :
81395.sol:
In Lassaigne's test, an organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The elements present in the organic compound, such as nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens, are initially present in covalent form.

During the fusion process, these elements react with sodium to form ionic sodium salts. For example, nitrogen and carbon form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), sulphur forms sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$), and halogens form sodium halides ($\text{NaX}$).

Therefore, the elements are converted from covalent form to ionic form.

Answer: covalent form to ionic form

82726.text: A hollow cylinder has a charge $q$ coulomb within it. If $\phi$ is the electric flux in units of voltmeter associated with the curved surface B, the flux linked with the plane surface $\mathrm{A}$ in units of voltmeter will be

By Gauss Law, total flux through the cylinder is given by:

Step 2: Flux through plane surface \(A\)
As surfaces \(\mathrm{A} \& \mathrm{C}\) is symmetrical so \(\phi_{\mathrm{A}}=\phi_{\mathrm{C}}\)
\(\phi_{\text{total }}=\phi_{\mathrm{A}}+\phi_{\mathrm{B}}+\phi_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{o}}} \quad [\text{Using Equation (1)] }\)
Given Flux through curved surface \(\phi_B=\phi\)
So,
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \phi_A+\phi=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0} \\
& \Rightarrow \phi_A=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}-\phi\right)
\end{aligned}\)$

84343.subject: Zoology
84343.text: Duodenum has characteristic Brunner's gland which secrete two hormones called:
84343.sol:
Brunner's glands are present in the duodenum region of small intestine. They secretes two hormones secretin and cholecystokinin. Oestrogen is secreted by ovary. Progesterone is secreted by corpus luteum. Prolactin is secreted by anterior pituitary. Parathormone is secreted by parathyroid gland.
Related Theory
Brunner's glands are located in the submucosa of the duodenum. They secrete an alkaline fluid containing mucin, which protects the mucosa from the acidic stomach contents entering the duodenum. It stimulates the release of digestive enzymes in the pancreas and stimulates the contraction of the gall bladder to empty bile into the duodenum.

84380.subject: Zoology
84380.text: Darwin in his "Natural Selection Theory" did not believe in any role of which one of the following in organic evolution ?
options: parasites and predators as natural enemies
84380.sol:
The theory of natural selection is based on the following factors :
(i) Rapid multiplication and limited food and space which leads to struggle for existence.
(ii) Struggle for existence and variations which leads to natural selection or survival of the fittest.
(iii) Natural selection and inheritance of useful variation over many generation which leads to formation of new species.
Darwin in his 'Natural Selection Theory did not believe in the role of discontinuous variation in natural selection. Darwin always believed in the universal occurrence of variation. In his opinion, variation is continuous in nature.
Related Theory
Because resources are limited in nature, organisms with heritable traits that favour survival and reproduction will tend to leave more offspring than their peers, causing the traits to increase in frequency over generations.

87397.subject: Chemistry
87397.text: A compound with molecular formula ${C}_{4}{H}_{10}{O}_{3}$ in converted by the action of acetyl chloride to a compound of molecular mass 190. The original compound $\left({C}_{4}{H}_{10}{O}_{3}\right)$ has how many $- \text{OH}$ groups?
87397.sol:
In acetylation, replacement of H of $O - H$ occurs by $C{H}_{3}CO -$ group. $- O - H + Cl \overset{O}{\overset{| |}{C}} - C{H}_{3} \to - OCOC{H}_{3} + HCl$

i.e., H atom of mass 1 amu is lost and an acetyl group of mass 43 amu is added. Thus, there is a net gain of 43 - 1 = 42 amu for every acetyl group introduced. Mass of difference of final product and original compound is 190 - 106 = 84.

Hence, number of $- OH$ groups $= \dfrac{84}{42} = 2$ .

91626.text: If $4$ distinct numbers are chosen randomly from the first $100$ natural numbers, then the probability that all $4$ of them are either divisible by $3$ or divisible by $5$ is
91626.sol:
Total cases $= {}^{100}{C}_{4}$

Numbers which are divisible by either $3$ or $5$

$= n \left(3\right) + n \left(5\right) - n \left(3 \cap 5\right)$

$= 33 + 20 - 6$

$= 47$

Favourable cases $= {}^{47}{C}_{4}$

Hence, required probability $= \dfrac{{}^{47}{C}_{4}}{{}^{100}{C}_{4}}$

Only $4$ possible cases

93120.text:
Four charges $+ q$,$+ q$,$- q$, and $- q$ are placed on $X - Y$ plane at the points whose coordinates are $\left(0. 5, 0\right), \left(0, 0. 5\right), \left(- 0. 5, 0\right) and \left(0, - 0. 5\right) respectively.



The electric field due to these charges at a point $P $\left(r, r\right)$, where $r > > 0. 5$, will be
93120.sol:
The four charges can be considered two dipoles of equal magnitude and directed along the +x axis and +y axis.
The magnitude of dipole moment = q x (distance between positive and negative charges on x-axis)

$p = q \times 1 = q$

The resultant dipole moment of these two dipoles with be, ${p}_{r} = \sqrt{q^{2} + q^{2}} = q\sqrt{2}$
The direction of the resultant dipole moment will be at $45 °$ from the x-axis
The distance of the point $( r, r )$ from the dipole is $r\sqrt{2} m$
The resultant electric field is

$E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{2{p}_{r}}{\left(r\sqrt{2}\right)^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{2 \times q\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}r^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{q}{r3}$

93378.text: In the arrangement shown in the figure, friction exists only between the two blocks, $A$ and $B$. The coefficient of static friction ${\mu}_{s} = 0.6$ and coefficient of kinetic friction ${\mu}_{k} = 0.4$, the masses of the blocks $A$ and $B$ are ${m}_{1} = 20kg$ and ${m}_{2} = 30kg$, respectively. Find the acceleration (in $m{s}^{- 2}$) of ${m}_{1}$, if a force $F = 150N$ is applied, as shown in the figure. [Assume that string and pulleys are massless]
93378.sol:
Let us assume that the two blocks move together, without slipping, relative to each other. The acceleration of the system in that case is

$a = \dfrac{Fcos60 °}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}}$

$a = \dfrac{150 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}{20 + 30} = 1 . 5m{s}^{- 2}$

In this case, if the frictional force acting between the two blocks is $f$, then writing the Newton's second law of motion, for the block of mass ${m}_{1,}$ we get

$T - f = {m}_{1}a$

$150 - f = 20 \times 1 . 5 = 30$

$f = 120N$

${f}_{max} = 0 . 6 \times 200 = 120N$

Since $f \le {f}_{max}$, our assumption about the two blocks moving together is correct and hence the acceleration of the blocks is $1 . 5m{s}^{- 2}$

Let Res be the distance of the earth from the sun. Hence, the intensity of radiation of the earth

$l ⁡ = \sigma T^{4} {R}_s^{2} / {R}_{es}^{2}$

$∴ 1 4 0 0 = \left(\text{5.6} \times 1 {0}^{- 8}\right) T^{4} {\left[\dfrac{\text{7.0} \times 1 {0}^{8}}{\text{1.5} \times 1 {0}^{1 1}}\right]}^{2}$

$T = 5801K$

96847.subject: Botany
96847.text:
How many of the following properties are seen in the brinjal plant?

Legume fruit, alternate phyllotaxy, actinomorphic flower, hypogynous flower, bicarpellary-syncarpous gynoecium, non-endospermic seeds
96847.sol:
Brinjal belongs to the family Solanaceae. The characteristics of Solanaceae are:

Habit: Mostly herbs and shrubs. Underground stem tubers are found in potato.
Leaves: In vegetative parts, alternate and floral regions, opposite
always exstipulate, simple, rarely pinnately compound as in potato and tomato.
Inflorescence: Cymose or solitary
Flower: Ebracteate, Pedicellate, complete, actinomorphic, bisexual.
Calyx: Consists of five sepals, gamosepalous, valvate. Sepals are usually persistent (e.g. brinjal, chilly, tomato, etc).
Corolla: Consists of five petals, gamopetalous, evaluate or twisted.
Androecium: Consists of five stamens, epipetalous altering with corolla lobes. Anther dithecous.
Gynoecium: Bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular, ovary superior and ovules are numerous on axial placentation.
Fruit: Berry or capsule.
Seeds: Many, endospermic.
Economic Importance: Many plants belonging to this family are a source of food (tomato, brinjal, potato), spice (chilli), medicine (belladonna, ashwagandha), fumigatory (tobacco), ornamentals (petunia).

97852.text: Sweet potato is a modified root. Potato is a modified stem. Both these plants are classified in order
97852.sol:
Ipomoea batatas or sweet potato is a plant which belongs to the family Convolvulaceae. It is also called the Morning glory Family. Potato belongs to the family Solanaceae. Both are included in the order Polymoniales.

Generally, order and other higher taxonomic categories are identified based on the aggregates of characters. Order is an assemblage of families that exhibit a few similar characters. The similar characters are less in number as compared to different genera included in a family. Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

97982.subject: Botany
97982.text: Solute potential of pure water and its solution are:
97982.sol: By definition," Water potential is the potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water in reference conditions." Thus, water will move from a higher water potential region to the lower potential region through the semipermeable membrane. It can be summarized as total of pressure potential, gravity potential and solute potential. Water potential of a fluid is reduced due to presence of solute as water molecules cluster around solute particles and this is referred to as solute potential. Pure water has the water potential of zero as there is no solute present and the pressure in the system is zero. Since, presence of solute particles reduces the water potential, thus, water potential of a solution will be less water potential of pure water that is less than 0.

99037.subject: Chemistry
99037.text: Which can be explained as applications of Le Chatelier's principle?
options: Transport of oxygen by haemoglobin in blood
Removal of $C{O}_{2}$ from tissues by blood
Tooth decay due to use of sweet substances
99037.sol:
(i) The haemoglobin of RBC combines with oxygen in lungs following the equilibrium,
${H}_{b} ( s ) + {O}_{2} ( g ) ⇌ {H}_{b}{O}_{2} ( s )$
When these are at lungs, the partial pressure of ${O}_{2}$ being appreciable show forward reaction, however when they pass to tissues, the partial pressure of ${O}_{2}$ decreases to favour backward reaction releasing ${O}_{2}$.
(ii) Removal of $C{O}_{2}$ from blood is based on the equilibrium,
$C{O}_{2} ( g ) + {H}_{2}O ( l ) ⇌ H^{+} ( aq ) + HC{O}_{3}^{-} ( aq )$
In tissues $C{O}_{2}$ gets dissolved in ${H}_{2}O$ due to high pressure whereas in lungs, the $C{O}_{2}$ is released out because of low pressure of $C{O}_{2}$.
(iii) Tooth enamel substance (Hydroxyapatite) $C{a}_{5} ( P{O}_{4}{)}_{3}OH$ shows the following equilibrium,
${\text{Ca}_{5} {{\text{(PO}_{4} \text{)}_{3} \text{OH}\overset{\text{Demineralization}}{⇌} {\text{5Ca}^{\text{2+}} ( \text{aq} ) \text{+}{\text{3PO}_{4}^{\text{3} -} ( \text{aq} ) \text{+}{\text{OH}^{−} ( \text{aq} )$
The use of sweet material or fermentation produces $H^{+}$. Which combines with $\overset{-}{O}H$ to favour demineralisation of enamel causing tooth decay.

The slope of a position-time graph represents the velocity (or speed, for uniform motion in one direction) of the object.

Let $v_X$ and $v_Y$ be the speeds of cars X and Y respectively.
We know that $v = \tan(\theta)$, where $\theta$ is the angle made with the time axis.

For car X:
$v_X = \tan(30^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Given the ratio of speeds:
$\dfrac{v_X}{v_Y} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Substituting $v_X$:
$\dfrac{1/\sqrt{3}}{v_Y} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\Rightarrow v_Y = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}$

For car Y:
$v_Y = \tan(\theta_Y) = \sqrt{3}$
$\Rightarrow \theta_Y = 60^\circ$

The angle made by the position-time graph of car Y with the time axis is $60^\circ$.

Answer: $60^\circ$

100686.text: A block is projected upwards along a rough inclined plane with an initial velocity of $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The angle of inclination of the plane is $30^\circ$ and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. The distance travelled by the block along the incline before coming to a momentary rest is (Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$)
100686.sol:
When the block moves up the incline, both the component of gravity along the incline and the kinetic friction act downwards along the incline, opposing the motion.

The magnitude of retardation of the block is given by:
$a = g \sin \theta + \mu_k g \cos \theta$

Substituting the given values:
$a = 10 \sin 30^\circ + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} (10) \cos 30^\circ$
$a = 10 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{3}} \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$
$a = 5 + 5 = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

Using the third equation of motion, $v^2 = u^2 - 2as$:
$0 = (10)^2 - 2(10)s$
$20s = 100 \Rightarrow s = 5 \text{ m}$

Answer: $5 \text{ m}$

100922.subject: Physics
100922.text: A car of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ accelerates uniformly from rest to a velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$ in $10\text{ s}$. The average power delivered by the engine during this time interval is
100922.sol:
According to the work-energy theorem, the total work done by the engine equals the change in kinetic energy of the car.

Initial kinetic energy, $K_i = 0$

Final kinetic energy, $K_f = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1000 \times (20)^2 = 200000\text{ J}$

Work done, $W = \Delta K = 200000\text{ J}$

Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken:

$P_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{200000\text{ J}}{10\text{ s}} = 20000\text{ W}$

$P_{\text{avg}} = 20\text{ kW}$

Answer: $20\text{ kW}$

101501.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion (A) : Steel is used in the construction of buildings and bridges.
Reason (R) : Steel is more elastic and its elastic limit is high. 

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
$A$ is not correct but $R$ is correct
101501.sol:
The relationship between Young's modulus, stress, and strain is:

$\dfrac{stress}{strain} = Y$

Since the elastic modulus of steel is more, for the same amount of stress, the strain will be less resulting in less deformation of buildings and bridges. Therefore, steel is used for construction of large structures. 

Hence, both assertion and reason are correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

102247.subject: Physics
102247.text: A hypothetical liquid has a molar mass of $22.4 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and a density of $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$. For any given mass of this substance, what is the ratio of the actual volume it occupies in the liquid state to the volume it would occupy if all intermolecular forces vanished at STP?
102247.sol:
Let us consider $1 \text{ mole}$ of the substance.
The mass of $1 \text{ mole}$ is $22.4 \text{ g}$.

The density of the liquid is $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, which is equivalent to $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ (or $1 \text{ g mL}^{-1}$).
The volume occupied by $1 \text{ mole}$ in the liquid state ($V_{\text{liquid}}$) is:
$V_{\text{liquid}} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \dfrac{22.4 \text{ g}}{1 \text{ g mL}^{-1}} = 22.4 \text{ mL} = 22.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}$

If all intermolecular forces vanish, the substance behaves as an ideal gas. The volume occupied by $1 \text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas at STP ($V_{\text{gas}}$) is $22.4 \text{ L}$.

The required ratio is:
$\dfrac{V_{\text{liquid}}}{V_{\text{gas}}} = \dfrac{22.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}}{22.4 \text{ L}} = 10^{-3}$

Answer: $10^{-3}$

102883.subject: Physics
102883.text:
A uniformly charged solid insulating sphere has a radius $R$ and total charge $+Q$. A narrow, smooth tunnel is drilled through its centre. A point charge $-q$ (where $q \ll Q$) of mass $m$ is released from rest at the surface of the sphere and allowed to fall through the tunnel. Its speed when it reaches the centre of the sphere is:
(Assume $\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of vacuum and neglect gravity)
102883.sol:
The electric potential at the surface of a uniformly charged solid sphere is:

$V_i = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{R}$

Initial potential energy of the charge $-q$ at the surface is:

$U_i = -qV_i = -\dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

The electric potential at the centre of a uniformly charged solid insulating sphere is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times the potential at the surface:

$V_f = \dfrac{3}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{R} \right) = \dfrac{3Q}{8\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

Final potential energy of the charge $-q$ at the centre is:

$U_f = -qV_f = -\dfrac{3Qq}{8\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

Applying conservation of mechanical energy ($K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f$):

$0 - \dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 - \dfrac{3Qq}{8\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{3Qq}{8\pi\epsilon_0 R} - \dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{Qq}{8\pi\epsilon_0 R}$

$v^2 = \dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 mR}$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 mR}}$

Note: Assuming the potential at the centre is the same as the surface (confusing it with a conducting shell) leads to zero speed, and assuming the potential at the centre is zero leads to incorrect energy changes.

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\epsilon_0 mR}}$

102922.text:
A uniformly charged spherical conductor of radius $10\text{ cm}$ has a total charge of $4 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}$. The magnitude of the electric field produced by this charge distribution at a certain point outside the sphere is $9 \times 10^{5}\text{ N C}^{-1}$. What is the distance of this point from the centre of the sphere?
$\left(\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}\right)$
102922.sol:
The electric field outside a uniformly charged spherical conductor at a distance $r$ from its centre is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{r^2}$

Rearranging for $r^2$:

$r^2 = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{E}$

Substituting the given values:

$r^2 = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 4 \times 10^{-6}}{9 \times 10^5}$

$r^2 = \dfrac{36 \times 10^3}{9 \times 10^5} = 4 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$

Taking the square root:

$r = 0.2\text{ m} = 20\text{ cm}$

Answer: $20\text{ cm}$

102923.subject: Physics
102923.text: Which of the following correctly describes the variation of the magnitude of the electric field $E$ with distance $r$ from the center of a uniformly charged hollow metallic sphere of radius $R$?
options: $E$ is zero for $r < R$, abruptly becomes maximum at $r = R$, and then decreases proportionally to $1/r^{2}$ for $r > R$.
$E$ increases linearly with $r$ for $r < R$, and decreases proportionally to $1/r^{2}$ for $r > R$.
$E$ is constant and non-zero for $r < R$, and decreases proportionally to $1/r^{2}$ for $r > R$.
102923.sol:
Inside a hollow metallic sphere, the charge resides entirely on the outer surface. Therefore, the electric field inside the sphere is zero ($E = 0$ for $r < R$).

Outside the sphere, the charge distribution behaves as if its entire charge is concentrated at the center. The electric field follows an inverse-square law, $E \propto 1/r^{2}$ for $r > R$.

At the surface ($r = R$), the electric field is maximum. Thus, the field is zero inside, jumps to a maximum at the surface, and then decreases as $1/r^{2}$ outside.

Answer: $E$ is zero for $r < R$, abruptly becomes maximum at $r = R$, and then decreases proportionally to $1/r^{2}$ for $r > R$.

107013.subject: Chemistry
107013.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107013.text:
Consider the following statements regarding ionization enthalpy:

(I) The first ionization enthalpy of Beryllium is greater than that of Boron.
(II) The second ionization enthalpy of Sodium is lower than that of Magnesium.
(III) The first ionization enthalpy of Nitrogen is greater than that of Oxygen.
(IV) First ionization enthalpy generally decreases from left to right across a period.

How many of the above statements are correct?
107013.sol:
Let us evaluate each statement:

Statement (I) is correct. Beryllium ($1s^{2} 2s^{2}$) has a fully filled 2s subshell, which is more stable and has a greater penetration effect than the $2p^{1}$ electron in Boron ($1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{1}$). Thus, Be has a higher first ionization enthalpy than B.

Statement (II) is incorrect. After losing one electron, Sodium forms $\text{Na}^{+}$ which has a highly stable noble gas core configuration ($1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6}$). Magnesium forms $\text{Mg}^{+}$ ($1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{1}$). Removing a second electron from the stable core of $\text{Na}^{+}$ requires much more energy than removing the 3s electron from $\text{Mg}^{+}$. Thus, the second ionization enthalpy of Na is much higher than that of Mg.

Statement (III) is correct. Nitrogen ($1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{3}$) has an exactly half-filled 2p subshell, which confers extra stability. Oxygen ($1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{4}$) has paired electrons in one 2p orbital, leading to electron-electron repulsion. Hence, N has a higher first ionization enthalpy than O.

Statement (IV) is incorrect. First ionization enthalpy generally increases (not decreases) from left to right across a period due to the increasing effective nuclear charge.

Therefore, exactly 2 statements (I and III) are correct.
